arenaGuard1.text: This is the way to the way in. The GATE is up the road, and the fox holding it asks a question you want to have an answer to before you get there.
Whether you are READY. Say yes and you are on the card. Say anything else at all and you are walking back down the carpet.
I have watched foxes stand on that spot and think about it for an hour. Nobody minds. Nobody forgets, either.

arenaGuard2.text: Do you walk this all day?
Up and back. Four hundred paces each way, and I have counted them more times than I am going to admit to a stranger.
Purses, mostly. A fight day puts a thousand of them on one road and about six foxes who came for exactly that.
And the ones coming back DOWN early. Those I look at properly. A fox who leaves before the card is finished has usually left something behind him.

arenaRoadGuard1.text: The road is open. The GATE is not — that is my colleague at the tunnel and he is stricter than I am.
What do you two do out here, then?
We stand where the market stops. Below us it is stalls and juggling; above us it is the King's ground. Somebody has to be the line.
Keep to the cobbles and we will never say a word to you.

arenaRoadGuard2.text: Every day this road looks the same and every day I have to look at it as if it does not.
Once. A fighter came back DOWN the carpet mid-card, straight past me, would not say why. Never entered again.
My orders are about who goes UP. Nobody ever wrote me one about who comes back. I have thought about that a lot since.

marla.text: Is there a fight on today?
There is always a fight on. Whether there is a TOURNAMENT is the question, and the King calls those when he pleases.
Since I was a kit. My mother sold ribbons on this ground and I stood on a crate to watch over the heads.
Three rounds, always three. LASERGUN, then STAFF, then SWORD — and they get closer to you every round. That is the joke of it. By the end there is nothing between you and them.
Who was the best you ever saw?
A quiet one. Never gave a name. Went through all three without taking a mark and walked out the west gate before the King could give the speech.

odo.text: You look like you have money on something.
I have money on EVERYTHING. That is the trade. Ask me the odds on any fox who ever went through that arch.
Go on, then. Odds on me?
Ha! Long. No offence — they are long on everybody. The drones take the first round and most foxes never see the second.
Here is the thing nobody bets on, though: it is not the SWORD round that finishes people. It is the STAFF. Everybody trains for the blade and nobody trains for the pole.
Noted, he says. Come back and tell me if I was right and I will stand you a drink at the tavern.

wren.text: You do not look like you are enjoying yourself.
I came to watch. I have watched. I am not sure I want to watch any more.
The DRONES are the worst of it. They do not tire and they do not flinch and they do not care who you are. Six of them, and they come at you all at once.
They say the King builds them himself. I do not know if that makes it better or worse.
Somebody does. I just hope it is somebody who comes back out. Not everyone has.

pell.text: Quiet as a grave until the horn goes, then a hundred foxes want a pie at once. That is this ground all over.
You must hear a lot, standing here.
I hear all of it. Who is fighting, who is frightened, who has told their family they are only coming to watch.
And I will tell you what I hear most. Everybody who walks up that road is sure they have a plan. Nobody who walks back down it says the plan survived.
Eat something first. That is my advice and it is better than most of the advice you will get out here.

tam.text: Older than the wall round it. This was a THRESHING FLOOR, long before anyone thought to charge for a seat.
Flat, hard, and big enough for the whole valley to stand on. When the harvests failed the floor stayed, and foxes being foxes, they found another use for a flat place with room for a crowd.
The first bouts were settlings. Two families, one argument, no blades — you went until one sat down. King Might's grandfather put the wall up and the rest followed the wall.
Ah. Now that is a longer story than a stallholder should tell for free. But look at the medallion on the road when you cross it, and count the points.

vance.text: I am the arena, as far as paperwork goes. Names in this book, bouts on that card, and the King's seal at the bottom of both.
Then you want the tunnel, and you want to know one thing before you get there. The fox holding it will ask if you are READY.
He is not making conversation. That is the rule, and the rule has exactly one door in it — you say yes, or you go back down the carpet.
And if I am not ready?
Then come back when you are. Nobody has ever been thrown out of this yard for taking an afternoon over it.
First blood, since the SETTLINGS. Eleven bouts and a closer. Winner is presented to KING MIGHT on the floor, which is the only reason anyone here still enters.

torv.text: The card. Eleven bouts and a closer, and I have read it four times walking up this road.
A name I know. There never is one. They put the strangers first and the strangers are the ones who last.
Word is there is an OUTSIDER on it this season. No house, no trainer, walked in off the road.
And I have got a copper on him, which my wife does not know about. Do not tell her, she runs the fruit stall.

sela.text: For the GATE, not the arena. There is a stone in the tunnel wall with names on it and I put something under it every season.
Everyone who did not walk back out. It is a short list now — they changed the rules after the SETTLINGS, first blood and done.
My brother is on it, from before that. He was very fast and not very careful, and one of those is enough.
Be careful instead. That is worth more to me than being sorry.

hetty.text: Good day for FISH. Everyone up here is selling pie and beer, so I walk down to the water and buy the one thing nobody thought of.
It works on the fighters. They will not eat pastry before a bout — sits on you, they say. So they come to me and pay whatever I ask.
That is the whole trick of a fight day. Sell to the ones who cannot eat what everybody else is eating.

rosk.text: Five, when there is a crowd. Four, when there is a crowd and I have had a drink.
I work the QUEUE. Nobody watches a juggler once the gate is open — they watch the gate. So I get them while they are still waiting.
And I will tell you what I have learned, standing here twenty years. You can pick the ones who will do well.
They are the QUIET ones. The loud ones are talking themselves into it. The quiet ones decided at home.

ivy.text: Whatever the orchard gave me. Take one — no, take one, I mean it. Nobody buys fruit on a fight day.
Pies and beer and little red flags. Nobody comes to an arena to eat sensibly.
My grandmother sold out of this same basket, mind. Back when the King's grandfather held the SETTLINGS here and there was no wall at all.
It was quieter. Two foxes, one argument, and everybody home by supper. Now they build things that do not bleed and we all pretend that is progress.
